policy.rule: Minutes must name dissenters when a motion is not unanimous. Present voting members must vote unless conflicted; a member not indicating a vote is deemed affirmative. Inference requires a source-verified per-vote roster, complete bounded official minutes, resolved dissent and no conflicting tally/exception. CARRIED alone is insufficient.
policy.pre_2021_policy: No default Yes inference until historicalBylaw819 recording convention is verified. Explicit unanimous full ballots can be supported separately when per-vote roster is validated.
policy.limitations: Minutes convention is documentary evidence, not audiovisual confirmation. Nonstandard motions, ambiguous identities/events, missing or partial sources, unresolved opposition and inconsistent membership/tallies are held.
policy.future_policy: Do not infer meetings after enabled_through without refreshing the official bylaw index and checking subsequent amendments or repeal.

committee_of_the_whole_scope.basis: Council Body includes COTW; section 4 applies all provisions; section 56 defines Council sitting as COTW, providing guidance or recommendations only.
committee_of_the_whole_scope.constraints: Official header and catalog must identify Committee of the Whole; every per-vote voter requires dated Council membership. Recommendations are not Council adoptions. Other committees remain held.

               4.1    BYLAW NO. 2044

                      The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2044 at 5:35 pm.





Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Kelsey Waller has applied on behalf
of 2621 Sooke Developments Ltd. to amend the zoning of 2621 Sooke Road and 3260
Jacklin Road from the One- and Two-Family Residential (R2) Zone to the Residential
Townhouse (RTl) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately 92
townhomes.

In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

1.   That as a bonus for increased density:

     a.    $2,074 per unit to the General Amenity Reserve Fund; and

     b. $610 per unit to the Affordable Housing Fund.

2. That frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan and a construction
   parking and traffic management plan are provided to Bylaw 1000 standards to the
   satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of a Building Permit;
     and

3. That prior to BylawAdoption, a subdivision plan that includes the required road
     dedication, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighbourhood and
Neighbourhood Centre designation.

Notifications and advertiisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

This rezoning should include a covenant that indoor parking spaces will be kept clear of
storage so as to be used for parking.

Mayor Young called a first time for presentations.

The applicant. Abstract Developments, gave a presentation on the proposal, outlining
the site characteristics, neighbourhood consultation process, and the project designs.

J. Bradlev, 2638 Alderglen PI. expressed opposition to the proposed project, expressing
concerns about the high level of density and impacts to wildlife.

A. Spargo. 1013 Gala Crt, expressed support for the proposal, noting that it is a good fit
for the area.

B. Cubit. #103-2745 Veterans Memorial Pkwv, expressed support for the proposal.

M. Degagne, 1037 Boxcar Cl. expressed support for the proposal, noting that it would
help first-time homeowners and that the location is fitting for the proposal.

I. Philips. 3509 Mvles Mansell Rd. expressed support for the proposal, noting that the
impacts to current residents would be minimal and that there would be net benefits to
the community.

M. Wagner. #104-2669 Deville Rd. expressed concerns about the density to the area and
would like retention of mature trees.




      T. Baldwin. 2642 Alderglen PI. expressed concerns about the proposed density.
      L. Webb. 2669 Mill Pond Ter. expressed support for the proposal and the additional
      housing that it would create.

      I. Davkin. 2618 Ernhill Drive, expressed concerns about the proposed density and innpact
      to trees.


      S. Koloiian, 896 Rowils Cr. expressed support for the proposal.

      N. Everett. 2611 Sooke Rd. expressed concerns about the proposed density.

      Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

      None presented.

      Mayor Young called for a third and final time for presentations.

      R. Larose. 3260 Jacklin Rd. expressed support for the proposal.

      The Mayor declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2044 closed at 6:12 pm.
      Mayor Young left the meeting at 6:15 pm. due to a perceived conflict with Item 4.2.

4.2   BYLAW NO. 2052

      Acting Mayor Wade opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No.2052 at 6:13 pm.

      Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Chad Bryden has applied on behalf
      of Darlene & David Smith, Limona Construction Ltd, Thomas Gruber, and Carol &
      Andrew Mack to amend the zoning of 829, 831, 835, and 839 Hockley Avenue from the
      R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential) Zone and RM3 (Apartment) Zone to the CCl (City
      Centre) Zone.

      This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of two six-storey
      apartment buildings.

      In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a
      bonus for increased density:

      1. $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; and
      2. $2,850 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund,

      Subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the
      Affordable Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy

      3. That the applicant also agrees to provide, prior to bylaw adoption, a Section 219
         covenant, registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees to the
         following:

          a.   That frontage improvements, a stormwater management plan and a
               construction parking and traffic management plan are provided to Bylaw 1000
               standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance
               of a Building Permit;





    b. That the developer will connect and be responsible for any upgrades required
         to the services and utilities required for the development;

    c. That no occupancy permits shall be issued until the roundabout at Peatt Road,
       and Hockley Avenue has been completed and is operational, to the satisfaction
         of the Director oif Engineering;

    d. That the building be strata titled into individual residential units prior to the
       issuance of an occupancy permit, to the satisfaction of the Approving Officer;

    e. That the developer consolidate the parcels into a minimum of two lots in
       accordance with the CCl zone regulations, prior to the issuance of a
         development permit;

    f.   That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for
         the proposed residential building(s) that ensures parking is allocated to each
         unit and visitors as required by the zoning bylaw and is not provided in
         exchange for compensation separate from that of a residential unit; and
    g. That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parkingspaces, shall
       feature an energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 charging or higher to
         the parking space; and

         1. Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle charging;
         2. Where an electric vehicle energy management system is implemented (load
            sharing), a qualified professional may specify a minimum performance
             standard to ensure a sufficient rate of electric vehicle charging; and

         3. The owner is required to keep the Electric Vehicle Servicing Equipment
            (EVSE) in operation and the Strata Council may not prevent an owner,
            occupant, or tenant from installing the EV charging equipment.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan City Centre designation.
Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local
Government Act.

Acting Mayor Wade called a first time for presentations.

The applicant gave a presentation on the proposal, providing an overview of the project
components, design, and location.

S. O'Sullivan. 821 Hocklev Ave. expressed concerns about parking and potential impacts
to trees.


Acting Mayor Wade called a second time for presentations.

R. Stoerzer. #7-848 Hocklev Ave, expressed concerns about traffic, parking, and
pedestrian safety.

M. Wagner. #104-2669 Deville Rd, expressed concerns about the lack of proposed green
space.





             Acting IVIayor Wade called for a third and final time for presentations. There being none,
             he declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 2052 closed at 6:31 pm.

             Mayor Young returned to the meeting at 6:34 pm.
